hero.eyebrow: Agent API · Schema Inspector · Column sort & search
hero.lede: A billion people program logic inside spreadsheets every day. They've never had a framework. NextSheet is it: components, end-to-end types, version control in Git, deploy to any surface.

thesis.p1: The spreadsheet is the most successful programming model ever shipped. It runs the world's finances, operations, science, and supply chains. It is the default interface humans reach for when data needs structure. And it scaled to a billion users without a framework, without a component model, without a type system, and without a deploy target.
thesis.p2: Every other software discipline had its inflection point. The web got React. Backend got Rails, then Next.js, then the edge. Data got dbt. Design got Figma. The spreadsheet — the single most-used piece of structured software on Earth — still authors the same way it did in 1985.
thesis.p3: <green>NextSheet is the bet that this ends now.</green> We're building the open-source framework for writing sheets like modern software: components, end-to-end types, composition from primitives, version control in Git, deploy to any backend, authored by humans and agents alike. One codebase, any surface.

gettingStarted.h2: From zero to a typed .xlsx in <accent>30 seconds</accent>.
gettingStarted.p: A single dependency. Local-first authoring. Compiles to every surface — Google Sheets, Excel Online, .xlsx, .csv — from the same source.

howItWorks.h2: One pipeline, five primitives, infinite surfaces.
howItWorks.p: NextSheet doesn't replace Excel or Sheets. It treats them as compile targets, the same way Next.js treats the browser as just another one. You write components. The compiler resolves references, types the cells, and emits for whatever surface you ask.
howItWorks.node1_d: JSX with types, business rules as pure functions.
howItWorks.node2_d: Analyzes dependencies, detects cycles, freezes evaluation order.
howItWorks.node3_d: Google Sheets API · Excel OOXML · .xlsx binary · .csv · JSON. One AST, five backends.
howItWorks.node4_d: If amount is currency, adding it to a string is a compile error — not a #VALUE! at 3 AM.
howItWorks.node5_d: Change the code, the production .xlsx updates. Git as the source of truth, not the file.

backends.h2: Write once. Deploy where the business already is.
backends.p: The CFO opens Excel. Marketing opens Sheets. Finance lives in audited PDFs. NextSheet compiles to every surface where your users already work — without migrating them to a new product.
backends.b1_desc: Bidirectional sync via OAuth. Native formulas, not images. Collaborators see cells — not code.
backends.b2_desc: Microsoft Graph. Push to SharePoint or OneDrive. Works with corporate accounts without add-ins.
backends.b3_desc: OOXML binary generated at build. Ideal for emails, reports, offline distribution, and auditing.
backends.b4_desc: Flatten to tabular, ready to ingest into BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift. Auto-escape, UTF-8 encoding.
backends.b5_desc: Deploy to the NextSheet hosted platform. Shareable URL, diff per PR, ephemeral preview.
backends.b6_desc: Fluent WorkbookBuilder + applyPatch(). JSON schemas for LLMs. toAnthropicTools() / toOpenAITools().

agentSection.p: NextSheet's Agent API gives LLMs a typed, structured interface to read, modify, and reason over your workbooks — not raw file bytes. Every operation is auditable, reversible, and formula-aware.
agentSection.cap1_desc: Ask questions about your workbook and get answers with cell-level citations — row index, column name, and sheet included.
agentSection.cap2_desc: Update assumptions while preserving formula dependencies. The agent patches values without touching the formulas that depend on them.
agentSection.cap3_desc: Debug errors and identify their root causes. The agent traces #VALUE!, circular refs, and broken dependencies back to their source cells.
agentSection.cap4_desc: Build new models or fill existing templates. Describe what you need in plain language — the agent writes typed Sheet components.
agentSection.cap5_desc: Navigate complex multi-tab workbooks seamlessly. The agent resolves cross-sheet references and follows data across sections.
agentSection.cap6_desc: Use connectors to bring context from your other tools directly into your spreadsheets — CRMs, databases, APIs.
agentSection.chat_q1: What's driving the MEA decline in row 5?
agentSection.chat_a1: MEA (row 5, sheet Sales) is down -3.1% YoY. The issue is in C5 (price: $199) — flat while volume dropped. D5 and E5 confirm the margin compression. Suggest reducing price to stimulate demand.
agentSection.chat_a2: Applied. D5 updated to $230,180. Formula in E5 recalculated automatically — dependency chain preserved.

charts.p: A NextSheet <Chart/> emits as a native chart on the target surface: editable in Sheets, interactive in Excel, SVG in the browser. Same component, five destinations.

deploy.h2: Git is the source of truth. Not the file.
deploy.p: Every change is a PR. Every release is a tag. Every rollback is a git revert. Finally, your financial models stop living in model_FINAL_v7_JUAN_vdef.xlsx.
deploy.card1_p: Cell-level diffs, not bytes. Tests over formulas. The reviewer sees which number changed and why, not a binary blob.
deploy.card2_p: Every pull request generates an ephemeral .xlsx, a disposable Sheet, and a shareable URL. Your CFO reviews the model before it reaches main.

roadmap.p: Today v0.4 is stable for Sheets, Excel, and .xlsx, with Agent API for LLMs. The next quarters build toward v1: typed formulas, collaborative runtime, and a delivery engine.
